'''Kashkari:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of California|Governor]] | before_election = [[Jerry Brown]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Jerry Brown]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | map_size = 302px }} {{ElectionsCA}} The '''2014 California gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of California]], concurrently with [[2014 California elections|elections]] for the rest of [[California executive branch|California's executive branch]], as well as elections to the [[2014 United States Senate elections|United States Senate]] in other states and elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[California Democratic Party|Democratic]] Governor [[Jerry Brown]] ran for election to a second consecutive and fourth overall term in office. Although governors are limited to lifetime service of two terms in office, Brown previously served as governor from 1975 to 1983, and the law only affects terms served after November 6, 1990.{{cite web|title=Summary of Qualifications and Requirements for the Offices of Governor and Lieutenant Governor |publisher=California Secretary of State Department |url=http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/statewide-elections/2014-primary/governor-lieutenant-governor-2014.htm |access-date=May 24, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706120012/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/statewide-elections/2014-primary/governor-lieutenant-governor-2014.htm |archive-date=July 6, 2014 |df=mdy }}{{cite web|title=Campaign Finance: Brown For Governor 2014|url=http://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/Campaign/Committees/Detail.aspx?id=1333789&session=2013|work=California Secretary of State|access-date=August 6, 2013}}{{cite web|title=Brown Shows Early Lead for 2014 California Gubernatorial Race|url=http://ivn.us/california/2013/08/05/brown-shows-early-lead-for-2014-california-gubernatorial-race/|work=IVN|access-date=August 6, 2013|archive-date=August 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130808051414/http://ivn.us/california/2013/08/05/brown-shows-early-lead-for-2014-california-gubernatorial-race/|url-status=dead}} A primary election was held on June 3, 2014. Under California's [[nonpartisan blanket primary]] law, all candidates appear on the same ballot, regardless of party. In the primary, voters may vote for any candidate, regardless of their party affiliation. The top two finishers — regardless of party — advance to the general election in November, even if a candidate manages to receive a majority of the votes cast in the primary election. [[Washington (state)|Washington]] is the only other state with this system, a top two primary ([[Louisiana]] has a similar primary). Brown and Republican [[Neel Kashkari]] finished first and second, respectively,{{cite web|title=Governor: Tim Donnelly congratulates Neel Kashkari|url=http://www.sacbee.com/2014/06/03/6455696/governor-neel-kashkari-leads-tim.html|work=IVN|access-date=June 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140604225558/http://www.sacbee.com/2014/06/03/6455696/governor-neel-kashkari-leads-tim.html|archive-date=June 4, 2014|url-status=dead}} which Brown won. He won the largest gubernatorial victory since [[1986 California gubernatorial election|1986]], "despite running a virtually nonexistent campaign."{{cite web|title=Jerry Brown Coasts To Re-Election With Nonexistent Campaign| date=November 5, 2014 |publisher=Huffington Post|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/11/04/california-governor-election-results_n_5819772.html|access-date=November 30, 2014}} This was the first time since [[1978 California gubernatorial election|1978]] that a Democrat carried Nevada County. ==Primary election== [[File:Neel Kashkari marching in the 2014 San Diego LGBT Pride Parade (1).jpg|thumb|right|Republican candidate Kashkari campaigns at the San Diego LGBT Pride Parade.]] A certified list of candidates was released by the secretary of state on March 27, 2014.
